title: A goal's evidence timeline
opening: Suppose a learner scores 6 of 10 on a usual task, then 8 of 10 on easier questions. Put the events and their conditions in order before deciding whether performance changed.

labels.interpretation: What does the later score establish?
labels.nextCheckGroup: Choose conditions for the next attempt
labels.practice: Apply it to one of your saved results

goal.current: 6 of 10 on the earlier usual-difficulty attempt
goal.rate: Unknown: the example has only one result on the usual difficulty.
goal.target: Not supplied. A target date is not a forecast.

events.title: Desired level recorded
events.detail: Aim for 8 of 10 on the usual difficulty. This is a target, not a prediction that it will happen by a particular date.

events.title: 6 of 10 correct
events.detail: Usual difficulty. This is the one comparable result in this scenario.

events.title: Practice recorded
events.detail: Practice precedes the later attempt. Order alone does not show that practice caused a change.

events.title: Instruction recorded
events.detail: Instruction precedes the later attempt. The timeline does not isolate its effect.

events.title: 8 of 10 correct
events.detail: The questions were easier. Record the score and the changed condition together; this result is not comparable to the earlier one.

interpretations.label: Mastery proven
interpretations.claim: Claim: the 8 of 10 proves rapid mastery.
interpretations.feedback: The later score is observed in this scenario, but the questions were easier. The changed condition makes the scores incomparable; the timeline does not establish rapid mastery or which event caused the result.

interpretations.label: Comparable progress unknown
interpretations.claim: Claim: the score rose, but progress on comparable tasks is unknown.
interpretations.feedback: This keeps the observed score, the easier questions and the conclusion separate. A later comparable task could clarify whether performance changed on the same scale.

nextChecks.label: Usual conditions
nextChecks.plan: Planned comparison: usual difficulty, same scoring rule. No result is recorded yet.

nextChecks.label: Easier set again
nextChecks.plan: Planned attempt: easier set. No result is recorded yet, so this would not settle the comparison with the usual-difficulty result.

practice.prediction: What goal are you tracking? Record its desired level, current level, observed rate and target date. Mark any value you do not know; a target date is not a forecast.
practice.observation: Add the date and conditions to one result you have already saved. If you have no result yet, say what you will record first.
practice.comparison: Which other goals or workloads compete for attention? What conditions must stay the same for the results to share a scale? Mark any causal link you cannot establish.
practice.result: Place actual practice, instruction, stage changes and comparison artifacts on the same timeline. Keep observed events separate from interpretations and planned future checks.
practice.revision: What does the timeline support? Revise the goal, forecast or practice conditions only where the dated evidence gives you a reason; keep unknowns unknown.
practice.step: Choose the next useful comparison. If a video or message would help, include it only with permission. State what result would change your account or simplify the timeline if it does not change a decision.

feedback.unavailable: Saving is unavailable for this lesson. Your notes remain on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete the goal, a saved result or first observation, comparison conditions, timeline evidence, revision and next step before saving.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved notes could not be loaded. Your current notes remain here.
feedback.conflict: These notes changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep these answers.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is still unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.

source.assessmentRole: The assessment record points to the retained community-config source body and has a different identity by design; it remains assessment-role evidence, not the current lesson body.
source.status: The four application actions and all listed limits/examples are preserved in source-actions.json. The timeline scenario and interaction are instructional illustrations, not observed learner outcomes. The recovered manuscript locator is p. 30; authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established.
